answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 18 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The dune multiplier is published, charged in reef, and inlet lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 2579 identities would post 3609 proofs and burn roughly 11 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
